title: Self-host n8n with Docker + Caddy
description: A production n8n stack with automatic HTTPS and persistent workflow storage on a $5 VPS.
overview: This guide walks through deploying a self-hosted n8n instance behind Caddy on a single low-cost VPS, with automatic TLS and workflows persisted to disk so a redeploy never wipes your data.
prerequisites: A VPS running Ubuntu 22.04 or later with at least 1GB RAM
A domain name pointed at the VPS's IP address
Docker and the Docker Compose plugin installed
Basic familiarity with the command line

steps.title: Provision the server
steps.content: SSH into a fresh Ubuntu VPS and install Docker and the Compose plugin.

code.code:
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
sudo apt install -y docker-compose-plugin

steps.title: Create the project directory
steps.content: Set up a folder to hold the Compose file and persistent volumes for n8n and Caddy.

steps.title: Write the Compose file
steps.content: Define two services: n8n on an internal port, and Caddy as the reverse proxy handling TLS termination.

code.code:
services:
  n8n:
    image: n8nio/n8n:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - N8N_HOST=n8n.example.com
      - N8N_PROTOCOL=https
      - WEBHOOK_URL=https://n8n.example.com/
    volumes:
      - ./n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n

  caddy:
    image: caddy:2
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile
      - ./caddy_data:/data

steps.title: Configure Caddy
steps.content: Caddy handles certificate issuance and renewal automatically, so the config is a single reverse_proxy block.

steps.title: Launch the stack
steps.content: Start both containers in the background. Caddy requests a Let's Encrypt certificate on first boot.

steps.title: Verify persistence
steps.content: Restart the stack and confirm your workflows survive the restart, since they're stored in the mounted n8n_data volume rather than inside the container.

architecture: Traffic reaches Caddy on ports 80/443, which terminates TLS and proxies requests to n8n over the internal Docker network on port 5678. n8n's SQLite database and encryption key live in a bind-mounted volume, so the container can be recreated without losing workflows or credentials.
result: A production n8n instance reachable at https://n8n.example.com with a valid, auto-renewing certificate, and workflow data that survives container updates and VPS reboots.
